Build rich admin panels with zero HTML/CSS/JS. Register pages from Python, compose UIs with the component API, and the SDK renders everything.

@aiui.page() registers a page with the server dashboard.js fetches /api/pages and /ui-config.json once each on load, builds the sidebar automatically When a page is selected, it fetches /api/pages/{id}/data If the data contains _components, they render as real UI elements (cards, tables, etc.) The Chat page highlights code with highlight.js, which it loads from cdnjs.cloudflare.com the first time a reply contains a code block. A chat with no code never contacts the CDN; without internet access, code shows unhighlighted.
Pages without component layouts render as formatted JSON.

Pages are grouped in the sidebar by the group parameter: Parameter Type Required Description page_id str ✅ Unique identifier (URL-safe) title str ✅ Display name in sidebar icon str ❌ Emoji or icon character group str ❌ Sidebar group name description str ❌ Subtitle below the title

When style is set to dashboard, 16 built-in pages are auto-registered from the feature system: Page Group Description 🤖 Agents Agent Configured AI agents ⚡ Skills Agent Agent tools and skills 🖥️ Nodes Agent Execution nodes 📊 Overview Control System overview 📡 Channels Control Messaging channels 📋 Sessions Control Active sessions 📻 Instances Control Connected instances 📈 Usage Control Token usage analytics ⏰ Cron Control Scheduled jobs 📋 Jobs Control Async job queue ✅ Approvals Control Pending approvals 🔌 API Control API documentation ⚙️ Config Settings Runtime configuration 🔐 Auth Settings Authentication 📜 Logs Settings Real-time log viewer 🐛 Debug Settings Debug information Custom pages added via @aiui.page() appear alongside built-in pages.
Each agent card on the Agents page includes a ▶ Run button. Clicking it navigates to the Chat page with that agent automatically pre-selected in the agent dropdown.

The Run button reads the agent name from its data-id attribute It pushes /chat?agent= to browser history and dispatches popstate The dashboard's popstate listener calls selectPage('chat'), loading the Chat view Chat's render() calls loadAgents(), then checks URLSearchParams for ?agent= If found, it sets the dropdown value and currentAgentName, then cleans the URL

Every dashboard includes a Test All Features link at the bottom of the sidebar. It auto-discovers all registered features from /api/features and tests each endpoint, showing pass/fail results in a grid.

Endpoint Method Description /api/pages GET List all registered pages /api/pages/{id}/data GET Get page handler response /api/features GET List all registered features /plugins/plugins.json GET Style-aware frontend plugin list
The dashboard provides a JavaScript API for registering custom views from the client side.

Register a custom view renderer for a page ID. Parameter Type Description pageId string Page ID to handle (e.g. "my-custom-page") renderFn async (container: HTMLElement) => void Async function that renders into the container cleanupFn () => void Optional cleanup function called when navigating away

When a page is selected, the dashboard resolves views in this order: Custom registered views — window.aiui.registerView() (highest priority) Built-in view modules — views/ .js for built-in pages, from /api/shell/manifest: a page whose source is builtin (kind legacy or native) loads .js. A page an app (register_page / @aiui.page), a plugin or a dashboard-plugin folder provides never gets a built-in view, even under a built-in id: it renders its own content, in the dashboard style too. When the manifest cannot be read, every page /api/pages lists is tried by the same file name. Generic JSON viewer — Falls back to rendering _components or raw JSON

The dashboard picks its colour mode in this order: the viewer's choice, stored under aiui-theme-preference (light, dark or system; the Theme page and the app shell write the same key); the app's default: aiui.set_theme(dark_mode=True|False), else YAML site.theme.mode (light, dark, system) or site.theme.darkMode; the OS (prefers-color-scheme), when neither chose a mode (/ui-config.json then sends site.themeDefault: "system"). A change of the OS scheme or of the stored choice in another tab applies at once.
